title: KV rebuild coldstart stall - incident review and runbook draft
body:
Summary:

On 2025-01-09 at ~02:15 UTC we observed a sustained increase in host memory usage across a subset of serving hosts in us-west-2 running model shard workers. The symptom was progressive heap growth followed by OOM kills on three hosts over a 28-minute window. Traffic routing and autoscaler prevented customer-visible error rates for most tenants, but internal SLIs (p99 latency for system health checks and batch tail latency) spiked.

Why this is novel/unusual: the immediate trigger was a post-deployment host churn (kernel patch + instance restart) that caused a coldstart sequence where worker processes initiated a KV cache rebuild from spill files on disk. The rebuild path was recently modified in #4678 to parallelize segment reads, but a subtle ordering race between the rebuild coordinator and the background eviction thread produced a stall: the rebuild worker held the per-host rebuild lock while spawning N reader goroutines, and one of the readers hit a retry path that blocked trying to acquire a global spill-index lock. That global lock is also taken by the eviction coordinator when high-memory heuristics fire. In combination, the result was a deadlock-like stall where many rebuilds queued, background batching accumulated requests, and host memory ballooned as more and more prefetch/KV entries were allocated but never transitioned to the steady-state cache.

Detection timeline (high level):
- 02:14 UTC: rolling kernel patch finishes on 12 hosts, auto-restart begins for service agents (coordination: rolling_restarts/2025-01-09).
- 02:15 UTC: first host (h-uw2-3f7) finishes startup and begins KV rebuild paths. Telemetry shows rapid allocation in kv_rebuild.alloc_rate > 3x baseline.
- 02:23 UTC: Heap growth crosses 70%% on h-uw2-3f7; eviction heuristics kick in and eviction_coordinator takes global spill-index lock.
- 02:24 UTC: One rebuild reader hits retry loop due to transient I/O error and attempts to reacquire global spill-index while coordinator holds it -> reader blocked.
- 02:26 UTC: Another host begins rebuild; rebuild coordinator on that host waits for global lock but finds it held; rebuild coordinator retains host-level rebuild lock.
- 02:35 UTC: Batching queue lengths climb (microbatcher.inflight > safe_threshold) and tail latency p99 increases; downstream route-level metrics show increased token generation latency.
- 02:42 UTC: OOM kill on h-uw2-3f7 (pid 22134). Two more hosts follow by 02:55 UTC.

Short-term mitigation (what we did during on-call):
1) Re-routed latency-sensitive traffic away from the affected AZ to reduce load and prevent cascading rebuilds (evacuation playbook).
2) Issued remote restart of the serving agent lifecycler on affected hosts to break the rebuild lock (sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent; allowed a clean restart to drop in-memory partial allocations).
3) Disabled the parallelized rebuild code path via dynconfig flag feature.flag.kv_parallel_rebuild=false to force single-threaded rebuilds until the race is fixed. This reduced simultaneous lock contention and stopped further OOMs.
4) Temporarily raised the eviction aggressiveness threshold (eviction.threshold.mem_pct -> 0.6) to make background eviction free entries earlier while rebuilds were ongoing.

Immediate observations after mitigation:
- After disabling parallel rebuilds, rebuild throughput slowed but memory growth stabilized across the fleet.
- Recovered hosts showed their caches repopulated more slowly but without sustained heap growth.
- No additional customer-visible errors recorded after 03:30 UTC once the dynconfig propagated.

Root cause hypothesis (short):
A combination of the new parallelized rebuild implementation and an existing global spill-index lock in the eviction coordinator led to lock-order inversion under coldstart conditions. When I/O/read-retry paths occur, a reader may attempt to take the global lock while the rebuild coordinator still holds the per-host lock, and the eviction coordinator simultaneously holds the global lock. The resulting cycle causes rebuild readers to block while they still retain memory references from partial allocations, preventing the eviction thread from freeing memory and creating positive feedback until OOM.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Thread stacks from core dump show reader goroutines blocked on spill_index::lock while holding ~10 heap segments allocated by rebuild.
- Eviction coordinator logs show acquisition of global spill-index lock at the moment heap usage spikes on the host.
- Prior to #4678 we saw no correlated stalls on coldstart restarts in our canary fleet. The timing correlates with the canary-to-prod roll of the PR.

Reproduction notes (how to repro locally / test env):
- Steps to reproduce in staging:
  1) Provision a host with a large spill store (>= 200GB) and enable feature.flag.kv_parallel_rebuild=true.
  2) Populate spill files with multiple segments and pause the network or inject transient read errors into the segment reader (use toxiproxy to add errors).
  3) Restart redwood-agent to trigger cold rebuild.
  4) Simulate eviction pressure by firing mem-pressure events (use internal test harness: scripts/mem-pressure-sim.sh).
- Expected repro result: blocked reader goroutines and sustained heap growth until restart or dynconfig toggle.

Runbook draft: immediate steps for on-call (prioritized):
1) If multiple hosts in an AZ show rebuild spikes, enable traffic evacuation for that AZ via traffic-router task (routing: set capacity=0 for weight-living zone).
2) Roll the dynconfig flag to disable parallel rebuilds: feature.flag.kv_parallel_rebuild=false.   Confirm propagation to all agents.
3) If host memory > 85%% and eviction not shrinking memory, escalate to SRE lead and consider graceful restart of redwood-agent on affected hosts in staged fashion (restart sequence: stop-agent -> wait 30s -> verify process endpoint clean -> start-agent).
4) Avoid mass restarts while canary settings are enabled; prefer dynconfig toggle to reduce blast radius.
5) After remediation, mark the hosts for postmortem analysis and preserve core dumps and /var/log/redwood/kv_rebuild.log.* files.

Longer-term mitigations and action items (owners/due dates):
- Engineering (serving-runtime): Remove the global spill-index lock from the fast path; refactor to a lock-free (or fine-grained locked) metadata index. Owner: Evan Park. ETA: 2025-02-28.
- Engineering (serving-runtime): Add strict lock-ordering assertions and CI fuzz test that injects read errors during rebuild to detect inversion. Owner: Marta Alvarez. ETA: 2025-02-14.
- SRE: Add a dedicated coldstart monitor that correlates 'rebuild.start' events with 'alloc_rate' and fires an alert if alloc_rate stays >2x baseline for >5 minutes. Owner: Darren O'Neal. ETA: 2025-01-20.
- Product/Runtime: Add a dynconfig default that restricts parallel rebuild worker count based on host memory size and spill file profile. Owner: Priya Menon. ETA: 2025-02-07.
- Observability: Publish a dashboard tile that shows rebuild concurrency vs spill-index lock acquisition and a histogram of rebuild duration under failure injection. Owner: Observability team (linked artifact). ETA: 2025-01-24.

Follow-ups (playbook & checklist updates):
- Update the eviction coordinator runbook with explicit note: "Do not take global spill-index lock while any per-host rebuild lock is held; prefer try-lock + backoff strategy during rebuild windows."
- Create a small integration test in canary that rolls the rebuild change with simulated I/O errors.
- Add a recovery script (tools/rebuild-safe-shutdown.sh) that attempts to gracefully quiesce rebuild workers by signaling them to finish in-flight readers and drop partial allocations before a restart.

Appendix: useful commands / artifacts collected during incident
- To list blocked rebuild goroutines on host: sudo gdb -p <pid> --batch -ex "thread apply all bt" > /tmp/rebuild-stacks.txt
- Evacuation command used: infra/routing/evacuate_az --region us-west-2 --az us-west-2a --reason "kv-rebuild-stall"
- Dynconfig toggle: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://config.redwood/api/v1/feature -d 'key=feature.flag.kv_parallel_rebuild&value=false'
- Collected core paths: /var/crash/core.redwood-agent.* (archived to s3://redwood-incident-archives/2025-01-09-kv-rebuild)
- Key logs: /var/log/redwood/kv_rebuild.log.* (start/stop timestamps) and eviction_coordinator.log.*

Post-incident notes for blameless review:
- This was triggered during a routine kernel patch rolling restart; we should long-term avoid risky concurrency changes that expand the attack surface of coldstart code paths without targeted fault-injection tests.
- The dynconfig mechanism and traffic evacuation tools worked as designed and prevented a full regional outage.
- We should classify parallelized rebuilds as a high-risk change and require a staged canary with forced coldstart scenarios before global rollout.

Questions for the postmortem meeting:
- What short tests would have caught the lock inversion earlier?
- Can we automate the fault-injection scenarios as part of pre-merge checks?
- Should we change default behavior so rebuilds are conservative on hosts with large spill volumes?

Action log (who did what during incident):
- 02:18 UTC - Priya Menon: detected alloc spike; opened INC-9842 and paged SRE rotation.
- 02:22 UTC - Darren O'Neal: routed traffic away from affected AZ and increased eviction aggressiveness.
- 02:28 UTC - Evan Park: toggled dynconfig to disable parallel rebuilds and started staged agent restarts.
- 03:01 UTC - Marta Alvarez: collected core dumps and stacks, uploaded to incident archive, and created repro script for staging.

Status: follow-ups assigned, mitigation in prod, awaiting change PR to refactor locking.
